paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God lays a work on your heart, and He doesn't hand you the whole thing at once. Nehemiah saw the broken wall for himself first, quietly, in the dark, before he said a word to anybody (Nehemiah 2:11-16). Then he spoke up with the plain truth, "You see the trouble we are in," and gave them a plan: "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem…" (Nehemiah 2:17). He also told them about "the gracious hand of my God upon me," and they answered, "Let us start rebuilding" (Nehemiah 2:18).

Now look at who ended up on that wall. Priests, goldsmiths, perfumers, rulers and whole families each took a piece, and Shallum even had his daughters helping (Nehemiah 3:1, 8, 12). Many of them repaired the part right by their own house (Nehemiah 3:10, 28). I LOVE that, friend, because it means nobody had to build the whole wall, just the stretch in front of them. The Tekoites' nobles did not put their shoulders to the work, but the wall kept going up anyway (Nehemiah 3:5).

And when the mockers showed up, Nehemiah didn't argue about whose city it was. He said, "The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success" (Nehemiah 2:20). That's the whole secret of this passage, baker. God gives the work, God gives the success, and He lets us put our hands to it side by side. So what's the stretch of wall in front of YOUR house today? Go build that piece, and don't skip it just because somebody else is building the one next to you.
